kind: A screen by slope on the server's test bed, two seeds, 6,000 and 24,000 updates: sleep with gates that start closed, alone on the delayed bed and on the looped bed, at the bed's best rate.
why: Sleep (--stack-sleep 64, 79cf0a4) replays every window of 64 bytes through the stack, and gate cells decide in quarters how much of each stored cell the replay rewrites, as the hippocampus replays recent experience at rest. With gates that start half open it failed on the server's seeds (sleep_with_data.json: a mean lead of 0.0034 after 24,000 updates, one seed behind), the cost right after each window boundary, and on the loop it trails after 6,000 updates (lsl-6k 0.0048 and 0.0081 behind). Gates that start closed (--stack-sleep-keep 0.9, c519644) make sleep start as the stack without it, and a gate opens only where the gradient finds the replay's cell better. On the laptop's seed they lead the plain bed by 0.0061 after 24,000 updates [0.0052, 0.0070] and 0.0080 after 6,000 (sleep_closed_gates_screen.json, whose mark of 0.005 they pass), with -0.0042 on new contexts, the 76% of bytes where the stack's gap to the Transformer lies. Its reading sends them to two server seeds, alone and on the loop, the stack's depth at full size.

arms.sleep-closed: --stack-sleep 64 --stack-sleep-keep 0.9 --pulse-budget 226000 on the server's delayed bed (sched/bin/arm.sh stack) at 1.2e-3: the arm of the laptop's screen; 5,256,788 parameters, the plain bed's 5,249,060 and the gate cells
arms.loop-sleep-closed: --stack-loop 1,4,3 --stack-sleep 64 --stack-sleep-keep 0.9 --pulse-budget 528000: the looped bed of loop_with_data with the same sleep, its budget doubled as for loop_sleep in sleep_with_data

base: Plain: bed24-lr12-s1 1.486381, bed24-lr12-s2 1.492556, rd-base-6k-s1 1.621562, rd-base-6k-s2 1.628309. Looped: lp-24k-s1 1.466405, lp-24k-s2 1.467507, lp-6k-s1 1.605730, lp-6k-s2 1.605468. The same seeds, lengths and rate. Beside them the open-gated sleep of sleep_with_data (sl at both lengths, lsl-6k, and lsl-24k when scored).
runs: slc-6k-s1, slc-6k-s2, slc-24k-s1, slc-24k-s2, lslc-6k-s1, lslc-6k-s2, lslc-24k-s1, lslc-24k-s2: seeds 20001 and 20002 through sched/bin/arm.sh stack --lr 1.2e-3 --seed 2000X (and --steps 6000) with the arm's flags, on the code copy of f876392 (v18c, which holds c519644), on GPU 0 at priority 39, after every job queued for the window of 2026-11-25. They run when GPU 0 has room: a 24,000-update sleeping bed takes about 2.2 hours (four times the plain bed), a looped one about 5.3 hours (seven times the looped bed).
measure: arm.sh's score: experiments/eval_stream.py on the first 2,000,000 validation bytes as 16 unbroken streams after 8,192 lead bytes, averaged weights, bits kept; each run paired with the base of its seed and length (experiments/compare_stream_scores.py) and split by context (experiments/gap_by_piece.py, near 240, far 8,192); the 24,000-update runs also by place in the window (experiments/window_place.py); the pulses a byte.
reading: The shared reading of experiments/read_lead_study.py twice: sleep-closed against the plain bed (--base-long bed24-lr12-s1 bed24-lr12-s2 --base-short rd-base-6k-s1 rd-base-6k-s2 --arm sleep_closed slc-24k-s1 slc-24k-s2 --arm-short sleep_closed slc-6k-s1 slc-6k-s2) and loop-sleep-closed against the looped bed (--base-long lp-24k-s1 lp-24k-s2 --base-short lp-6k-s1 lp-6k-s2 --arm loop_sleep_closed lslc-24k-s1 lslc-24k-s2 --arm-short loop_sleep_closed lslc-6k-s1 lslc-6k-s2). An arm is a fix for late learning if after 24,000 updates its mean lead is at least 0.010 with both seeds ahead and the lead grew by at least 0.005 since 6,000; a constant gain if it leads by that much without the growth; otherwise it fails. If loop-sleep-closed is a fix or a constant gain, closed-gated sleep goes to full size on the lifted loop (fs-loop6-lift with and without it, 24,000 updates at 6e-4, in a record of its own written before those runs, which states their pulses and time); if only sleep-closed passes, it goes to full size on the plain stack the same way. If both fail and an arm's lead grows by at least 0.005 from 6,000 to 24,000 updates, that arm gets the pair at 96,000 updates in a record written then. Otherwise closed-gated sleep is reported and stops. Every claim states the pulses a byte, about twice the base's. The laptop's seed is reported beside these and never pooled with them.
seen_before_recording: sleep_closed_gates_screen.json's two runs (slc-6k-s3, slc-24k-s3) with their pairings and splits by context, recorded with this record; sleep_with_data.json's runs (sl at both lengths on two server seeds, lsl-6k on two, the laptop's sl-6k-s3 and lsl-6k-s3); the plain and looped bases. No server run with closed gates has trained; window_place and the gates' openings of slc-24k-s3 are not measured yet.
